wherein present applicants are facing trial for the offences punishable under Section 323, 504, 506, 498-A IPC and under Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station - Clementown, District - Dehradun.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the applicants that applicant no. 1 married with respondent no. 2 on 26.04.2021 at Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar, however, due to some differences they started living separately.

Subsequently, they came up to amicable settlement and applicant no. 1 had paid permanent alimony of Rs. 8,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakh only) to respondent no. 2 and respondent no. 2 also admits that she has received Rs. 8,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakh only) as permanent alimony.

It is further contended that thereafter, a divorce petition was filed by parties for mutual divorce under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act and the same was decreed on 20.11.2023.
6.

7. Present compounding application is supported by the affidavit of applicants and respondent no. 2 and they are duly identified by their respective counsel.

8. Though offences under Section 498A IPC and under Section 3 / 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
are not compoundable but in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs.
